test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: During a lathe operation, the influence of machining allowance on the total depth of cut taken is that:

options.text: it directly determines the depth of cut in each pass
it directly determines the feed rate corresponding to the speed
it sets the total material to be removed, which is then divided into multiple cuts
it has no influence on the depth of cut

solution:
The correct answer is __it sets the total material to be removed, which is then divided into multiple cuts**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Machining allowance__ is the total amount of material that needs to be removed during the machining process.
 
• It determines the total depth of material to be removed from the workpiece.
 
• The total material removal is divided into multiple passes or cuts to ensure a smooth finish and to avoid tool overload.
 
• Each pass may involve a specific depth of cut, feed rate, and speed based on the machining conditions and material properties.
 
• Machining allowance is a critical parameter in ensuring precision and achieving the desired dimensions of the final product.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Depth of Cut:**

 
 
• The depth of cut refers to the thickness of the material layer removed in one pass of the cutting tool.
 
• It is influenced by machining allowance but also depends on the tool's capacity and material type.
 
 
 
• **Feed Rate:**
 
 
• The feed rate is the speed at which the cutting tool advances into the workpiece.
 
• It is generally independent of the machining allowance but must be optimized for efficient machining.
 
 
 
• **Machining Passes:**
 
 
• Machining allowance is distributed across multiple passes to ensure the accuracy of the final product.
 
• Each pass removes a portion of the material to prevent tool wear and overheating.
